check_iban.description: Check that an IBAN is a real one before you pay it: its check digits, its length and its layout for the country it is from. For more than 60 countries it also returns the bank's name, BIC (SWIFT code), address and city, and it says whether the country is in SEPA. When the IBAN fails, the answer says why in plain words. No API key required.
check_iban.name: check_iban

parameters.description: The IBAN to check. Paste it however it was written: spaces, hyphens and lower case are all fine, and it is tidied up before it is sent.
parameters.name: iban

returns.description: One IBAN and everything IBAN Analyzer reports about it.

account_number.description: The domestic account number inside the IBAN, for example '0532013000'. Null when the IBAN is invalid.

bank.description: The bank the IBAN belongs to. Every field is null when IBAN Analyzer holds no record of it.

address.description: The bank's street address. Null when unknown.

bic.description: The bank's BIC (SWIFT code), for example 'COBADEFFXXX'. This is the code an international transfer asks for. Null when unknown.

city.description: The city the bank is registered in. Null when unknown.

found.description: True when IBAN Analyzer holds a record of the bank. False when the IBAN is invalid, or its country is one it has no bank register for.

name.description: The bank's name, for example 'Commerzbank'. Null when unknown.

postal_code.description: The bank's postcode. Null when unknown.

bank_code.description: The bank's own domestic code as it sits inside the IBAN, for example '37040044'. Null when the IBAN is invalid.

checksum_valid.description: Whether the IBAN's two check digits match the rest of it. This is what catches a mistyped or swapped character.

country_code.description: The two-letter code of the country the account is held in, for example 'DE'. Null when the IBAN does not name a country.

format_valid.description: Whether the letters and digits are laid out the way its country's IBANs are.

iban.description: The IBAN with spaces and punctuation removed and letters upper cased: the electronic form, and the one to store.

iban_formatted.description: The same IBAN in groups of four, the way it is written on paper: 'DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00'.

length_valid.description: Whether the IBAN is the right length for its country (22 characters for Germany, 18 for Denmark).

problem.description: Why the IBAN failed, in plain words, ready to show a person. Null when it is valid.

sepa_country.description: Whether the country is in SEPA, the Single Euro Payments Area, so the account can receive a SEPA transfer or direct debit. Null when the country is unknown.

valid.description: True when the IBAN passed every check: its check digits, its length and its layout for the country it is from.

check_ibans.description: Check a whole list of IBANs in one step (a payment file, a supplier list, a column from a spreadsheet) and get back each result, with its bank where known, plus the counts to branch on. A bad IBAN comes back as a row saying what is wrong, not as a failed step, and the invalid ones are gathered into their own list. Up to 50 at a time. No API key required.

results.problem: The check digits do not match the rest of the IBAN, so a character is probably mistyped.

check_ibans.name: check_ibans

parameters.description: The IBANs to check, up to 50 in one step. Each one counts towards the free limit of 60 checks an hour, though an IBAN listed twice is only checked once. Anything that fails (a mistyped digit, or a cell that is not an IBAN at all) comes back as a row saying so rather than failing the whole step.
parameters.name: ibans

all_valid.description: True when every IBAN is valid: the single flag to branch on before releasing a payment run.

count.description: How many rows the step returned.

invalid_count.description: How many of them are not valid.

invalid_ibans.description: Just the IBANs that are not valid: the list to put in front of a person.

results.description: One result per IBAN, in the order they were given. An entry that is not an IBAN at all gets a row too, with every check false and the reason in 'problem', so the rows line up with the list that was sent.

list_countries.description: List every country IBAN Analyzer checks IBANs for, with the two-letter code an IBAN from there starts with and whether it also returns bank details there. Use it to check a country is covered before building a workflow around it. This does not count towards the hourly limit. No API key required.

parameters.description: Only countries whose name contains this text, or whose two-letter code is exactly this. Not case sensitive. Leave it empty for all of them.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Return only the countries where IBAN Analyzer also returns the bank's name and BIC. Off by default.
parameters.name: bank_details_only

countries.description: The countries that matched, by name A to Z.

items.description: One country IBAN Analyzer checks IBANs for.

bank_details_available.description: Whether IBAN Analyzer holds bank details for this country, so a check there comes back with the bank's name and BIC.

description: Check IBANs and find the bank behind them. Check one IBAN or a whole payment file at once (the check digits, the length and the layout for its country) and get back the bank's name, BIC (SWIFT code), address and city for more than 60 countries, whether the country is in SEPA, and a plain-words reason when an IBAN is wrong. No account or API key required.
